exposure: Background data (not living with a partner, fear of giving birth, birth preference other than vaginal)
Birth outcomes (vaginal birth, epidural, augmentation, birth complication)
cohort: The study included 226 women in a rural area of Sweden who were offered continuity of midwifery care during pregnancy and birth.
finding: Women who received care from a known midwife in labour were more likely to have a positive birth experience, predominantly in the domain of Professional support.
mod_finding: Vaginal birth without an epidural, augmentation, or birth complications was associated with a better birth experience.
